rationale:
Evidence: all three raced designs (iterations 0, 1 and 3) left the track in every development trial, with finish rate 0. max_error sits at about 0.06 m in every race, which is the off-track limit for body_width 0.12 and cannot be raised within the allowed range. rms_error is about 0.03 and steering_oscillation is small (0.06 to 0.15), so the robot drifts steadily to the edge rather than jittering. Progress is almost identical across kp, kd, ki, sensor size and line-loss settings (0.04 on the s-bend in every race). Adding ki (iteration 3) changed the score by only -0.58, so integral action is not the fix. Iteration 2's wide 7-sensor array and iteration 4's lower speed were never raced, so both remain untested.

Changes: (1) Use the wide 7-sensor array at x = -0.075 to +0.075 (0.025 m steps), y = 0.06, sensor size 0.016. This keeps the tape visible out to about 0.09 m of offset, before the 0.06 m limit is reached. (2) Lower base_speed from 1.2 to 0.9 to test whether entry speed on the early bend is the failure point, and to give the steering more time to settle. (3) Keep kp 4.5 to match the halved signal per metre of offset from the wider array. (4) Raise kd from 0.4 to 0.8. The higher kp and lower speed raise the risk of overshoot, and extra damping should counter it. (5) Set ki to 0 to keep the test clean. Geometry otherwise matches iteration 1 (mass 0.6, wheel track 0.12, radius 0.03, body 0.12 x 0.16) and line_loss stays last_direction.

Expected result: the robot should hold the line through the early bend, so max_error should fall below 0.06 and progress should rise above 0.04 on the s-bend. Finishing within 3 s is unlikely at 0.9 speed. If tracking holds, the next revision should raise base_speed in steps toward 1.5 to 2.0.
